definition: Also known as OS or GUI agent paradigm, where multimodal LLMs are given the ability to directly interact with computer environments such as controlling mouse and keyboard.
details: Also known as OS or GUI agent paradigm, where multimodal LLMs are given the ability to directly interact with computer environments such as controlling mouse and keyboard.

explainer.lead: Computer use lets a multimodal language model operate a graphical computer interface, not just talk about it. By connecting what the model sees on screen to mouse and keyboard actions, it can work through tasks in ordinary computer environments.

tiers.eli5: Imagine showing a helper your computer screen and letting them use the mouse and keyboard for you. Computer use gives an AI a similar job: look at the screen, choose an action, and then look again to see what changed. It repeats this until the task is done or it gets stuck.
tiers.practitioner: An implementation typically runs an observe–act loop: supply the goal and a screenshot, emit a mouse or keyboard action, execute it, and return the updated screen. Check the environment state after actions rather than assuming a click or keystroke succeeded. Common pitfalls include clicking the wrong control, losing track after the interface changes, and stopping before the task is actually complete.
tiers.paperLevel: At step t, a multimodal policy π receives goal g and observation o_t, such as a GUI screenshot, and selects action a_t ~ π(g, o_≤t, a_<t), where a_t is a mouse or keyboard operation. The computer environment executes a_t and returns o_{t+1}, producing a closed-loop sequential decision process. Key difficulties include grounding visual elements in precise actions, recovering from errors, and judging whether the goal has been achieved.

explainer.example: To save an open document as a PDF, the agent inspects the screen, opens the File menu, chooses the export option, enters a filename, and confirms the dialog. It then checks the resulting screen before deciding whether another action is needed.

usedIn.name: Desktop task assistance
usedIn.detail: An agent works toward a user's goal by operating visible controls with mouse and keyboard actions.

usedIn.name: Graphical operating systems
usedIn.detail: Multimodal models interact with the GUI as an environment, using screen observations to guide subsequent actions.

explainer.intuition: Instead of requiring every application to offer a special text command or API, give the model the same broad interface a person uses: the screen, mouse, and keyboard. Its visual understanding guides action, and each new screen provides feedback for the next decision.
howItWorks: Receive a task goal and observe the current screen.
Interpret visible interface elements and decide the next action.
Execute a mouse or keyboard operation in the computer environment.
Observe the resulting screen and update the task state.
Repeat until the goal is complete or the agent cannot proceed.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turns a multimodal LLM from a system that only responds with text into one that can carry out sequences of actions in a GUI. The repeated screen feedback also lets later decisions depend on what earlier actions actually changed.
misconceptions: It is more than suggesting which button to click: the agent directly performs actions in the computer environment.
GUI control is not the same as calling an application's underlying API; this paradigm centers on screen interaction through mouse and keyboard.

nodes.label: Task goal
nodes.note: The outcome requested by the user.

nodes.label: Multimodal LLM
nodes.note: Combines the goal with visual observations to choose actions.

nodes.label: Mouse and keyboard
nodes.note: Carry out the selected GUI operation.

nodes.label: Computer environment
nodes.note: Executes actions and changes the interface state.

nodes.label: Screen observation
nodes.note: Shows the model the updated GUI.

diagram.caption: Computer use is a feedback loop: the model observes the GUI, acts through mouse and keyboard controls, and observes the result.
